title: Differential Equations for Living & Engineered Systems
description: Build, solve, and interpret first- and second-order differential equations, coupled systems, stability, and numerical integration for biological and robotic dynamics.

outcomes.description: Classify ODEs and choose solution methods.
Interpret equilibria, time constants, and stability.
Model coupled state variables as a vector system.
Check numerical solutions against physical constraints.

lesson_objectives.description: Solve separable and linear first-order ODEs.
Relate damping ratio to qualitative transient behavior.
Write a mechanical model from force balance.
Linearize a nonlinear system near an equilibrium.
Use eigenvalues to classify local stability.
Apply forward Euler and recognize its limitations.
Choose a step size based on stability and accuracy, not convenience alone.

workload.basis: Not measured. Legacy nominal credit and display-time labels are not retained as workload estimates.

lessons.title: First-order models and time constants
lessons.worked_example: A sensor response with τ=4 s reaches about 63% of its final step change after 4 s and about 95% after 3τ, under the first-order model.

lessons.title: Second-order systems and mechanical response
lessons.worked_example: For m=1 kg and k=100 N/m, ωn=10 rad/s. Critical damping is ccrit=2√(km)=20 N·s/m.

lessons.title: Coupled systems, equilibria, and stability
lessons.worked_example: In a two-state linear model with J=diag(−1,−3), perturbations decay independently with time constants 1 and 1/3 time units.

lessons.title: Numerical ODEs and error control
lessons.worked_example: For ẋ=−x, x₀=1, Euler with h=0.1 gives x₁=0.9; exact x(0.1)=e^(−0.1)≈0.905, showing a small first-step error.
